# Brief for the coach: program review and the change made on 2 November 2026

## The short version

I opened Joe's current program, checked it against the engine's latest rules, and found two things the newer engine now supports that the program had been working around: a priority lift can count its assistance variants toward its weekly set target, and a conditioning session can sit on the same weekday as a lifting session. I used both. The kettlebell swing finisher came out of Monday's overhead-press session and became its own optional swing session on Mondays, and the strict pull-up now has a real weekly set target that counts negatives and band pull-ups.

One thing you need to know up front: I did not stop at the preview. I ran the real adoption, so version 2 of the program is now recorded as in force, dated 2 November 2026. Nothing has reached Hevy — Hevy only changes when a week's plan is applied, and that step asks for a yes first — but the program itself is already written. If Joe doesn't want the swing session moved, the fix is a further amendment, not an undo. He should be told that plainly and asked whether he's happy with it.

## Where Joe stands

The engine's progress view, as of 2 November:

- Strict pull-up: best is 3 reps, on 29 March 2026. Target is 5; 2 to go. Last two tests (26 October and 1 November) were a single rep at RPE 10.
- Bench press: estimated one-rep max 174.9. Best logged set 160.94 for 3, on 14 April 2026. Target is 1.25 × bodyweight; 0.32 of a bodyweight multiple to go.
- Overhead press: estimated one-rep max 85.15. Best logged set 93.0 for 5, on 10 July 2026. Target 0.75 × bodyweight; 0.24 to go.
- Deadlift: no current estimate. Best logged set 200.0 for 5, on 11 April 2026. Target 2 × bodyweight; 0.9 to go.
- Back squat: estimated one-rep max 231.48. Best logged set 220.46 for 1, on 13 October 2026 (the 100 kg single at the PT). Target 1.5 × bodyweight; 0.32 to go.

No stall streaks and no resets on any of the five. All figures are in Joe's units, pounds.

Phase: maintenance, target rate 0.0 % of bodyweight a week, observed −0.13 % a week. The engine does not call the maintenance target met — he's drifting slightly down. The phase runs until you call it.

The block opened on 1 November has 0 hard weeks against a ceiling of 6, and no light week is pending. There are no closed weeks yet, so the dose view is empty for now.

## The program as it stood before the change

"Five compounds around the PT Tuesday", hypertrophy emphasis, home by default, A/B rotation. Thursday off.

- Monday · OHP, back and arms (75 min budget). Overhead press: warm-ups of 5 and 3, a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4 × 6 at 85 % of the top; 180 s rest. Dumbbell chest-supported row 4 × 8–12 at RPE 8. Lateral raise 3 × 12–15 and rear delt fly 3 × 12–15, both at RPE 8, as a pair. Kettlebell swing finisher 8 × 10 at RPE 7, one set at the top of each minute, starting at 40 lb — this is the line that moved.
- Tuesday · PT. Week A chest and back (about 6 chest, 6 lat, 3 biceps hard sets); week B legs and core (about 6 quad, 4 glute, 4 ab sets). Joe doesn't control content.
- Wednesday · Pull-up volume and core (75). Scapular pull-ups 2 × 6–8 at RPE 5 as activation. Negative pull-ups 3 × 2–4 at RPE 8 with a 4–5 s lower; once every set reaches 4, lengthen to 6 s, then 8 s, then add the vest. Band pull-ups 4 × 5–8 at RPE 8; at the top of the range on every set, move to a lighter band. Flexed-arm hang 2 × 20 s. Lying leg raise 3 × 10–15 and suitcase carry 4 × 30 s as a pair. Single-leg calf raise 3 × 10–15.
- Friday · Strict pull-up test, squat and legs (75). One strict pull-up single at RPE 10, same grip every time. Back squat: warm-ups of 5, 3 and 2, top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4 × 5 at 85 %; 180 s rest. Romanian deadlift 3 × 6–10 at RPE 8. Split squat 3 × 8–12. Seated dumbbell shoulder press 3 × 8–12 and single-leg calf raise 3 × 10–15 as a pair. Ab wheel 3 × 6–12.
- Saturday · Bench, back and arms (90). Bench: warm-ups of 8, 5 and 3, top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 4 × 6 at 85 %. Bent-over row 4 × 6–10. Incline dumbbell bench 3 × 8–12. Dip negatives 3 × 3–5 with the same lengthen-then-vest rule at 5 reps. Overhead triceps extension 3 × 10–15 and lateral raise 3 × 12–15 as a pair.
- Sunday · Deadlift and legs (90). Deadlift on the top-and-back-off scheme; farmers walk starting at 50 lb per hand (Hevy records 45.36 kg for the pair).
- Standing, optional: a kettlebell circuit (swing starting at 40 lb, 18.14 kg) and a daily hang.

Weekly set targets were 10 hard sets per muscle; per lift: bench 5, overhead press 5, deadlift 4, squat 5, and pull-up 1 — that 1 is what the change fixes. Deload policy: light week after at most 6 hard weeks, cut sets 40 %, keep the load, cap everything at RPE 8, test the priority lifts.

Time estimates against budgets (rest plus sets): Monday 58 of 75, Wednesday 39 of 75, Friday 65 of 75, Saturday 65 of 90, Sunday 65 of 90. Nothing over.

## What the change records

Version 2, an amendment — same block, same rotation position (week A for the week of 2 November), nothing reset. The differences from version 1:

1. **Monday holds two sessions in both rotation weeks:** the OHP lifting session, then a new optional conditioning session, "Conditioning · Kettlebell swing EMOM". The swing finisher line is removed from the lifting session. Monday's lift estimate drops from 58 to 47 minutes.
2. **The new swing session** runs on a density scheme: 12 minutes to start, one set at the top of every minute, 12 swings a minute at 40 lb (18.14 kg), target RPE 7, 20 s rest written on the line. When it comes in at or under RPE 7 the engine adds 2 minutes, up to a cap of 16 minutes; after that the reps per minute rise, capped at 15. It is optional, so it never counts against adherence and never fails a week; its done-count shows as a streak.
3. **The pull-up's weekly target is now 10 hard sets**, counting negative pull-ups and band pull-ups toward it. As written, Wednesday plans 3 negatives and 4 band sets — 7 — plus the Friday single, so the dose check will show him under 10 unless the week-plan adds sets or the circuit's swing-free pull-up work is counted. You may want to decide whether 10 is the right number or whether to settle at 8 (the engine's default for a lift).
4. **The old acknowledgement** for the pull-up target of 1 was removed because it no longer applies.
5. The reason recorded on the version: the newer engine lifts three cutover workarounds, so the pull-up gets a real target and the swings get their own session.

Start loads carried on the version: farmers walk 50 lb per hand (45.36 kg), swing 40 lb (18.14 kg) in both the new session and the circuit.

## What Joe logged on Monday 2 November

- Overhead press 68 lb: 5, 6, 8, 8, 8 reps at RPE 7.5, 6, 6, 6, 6. Estimated one-rep max 85.0. The plan called for a top 5 at RPE 8 and 4 × 6; he did 8s at RPE 6, so the load was too light and the next prescription should move up.
- Chest-supported row 20 lb per hand: 6, 12, 12 at RPE 8, 7, 7.5. Only three sets logged of the four planned.
- Lateral raise 5 lb per hand: 15, 15, 15 at RPE 6, 6, 7.5 — top of range, ready to go up.
- Rear delt fly 7.5 lb per hand: 15, 15, 15 at RPE 6, 7, 8 — top of range, ready to go up.
- Kettlebell swing 40 lb: 8 × 10, RPE 7 on the first six, 7.5 on the last two.
- Daily hang logged, no figures.

Pull-up history since September: 27 September band pull-ups 5, 5 at RPE 6. 26 October negatives 2, 2 at RPE 8 and 9; band pull-ups 6, 5, 5 at RPE 8.5; strict single at RPE 10. 1 November band pull-ups 6, 6, 5, 4 at RPE 8, 8.5, 9.5, 10; strict single at RPE 10.

## Warnings on the adopted program, and what they mean

Three, two of them left standing on purpose with a written reason frozen on the version:

- **Deadlift target of 4 sits below the 5–15 band for a priority lift.** Before the change this same warning fired for the pull-up at 1; now that the pull-up is at 10, the deadlift is the one outside the band. I left it with this reason: Sunday's deadlift plans exactly 4 hard sets (the top set and three back-offs), Friday's Romanian deadlift carries the hinge, and the PT sometimes adds deadlifts on Tuesday; a target of 5 would show him under target every week the session is done as written. For training it means nothing changes. To clear it instead: raise the target to 5 and add a back-off set on Sunday, or count the Romanian deadlift as a variant.
- **The strict pull-up single uses a hold scheme, which the engine does not expect on a priority lift under this emphasis.** Left, same reason as before: the single is the weekly measure while his max is 1; negatives and band pull-ups do the building; the strict line becomes real work once the test passes about 5. Clears when the line moves to a progressing scheme at that point.
- **One pushed Hevy routine differs from the plan in force** (not left): three rep fields on the first exercise's sets 5, 6 and 7, and the weight on the second exercise's sets 1, 2 and 3 have been edited in Hevy. It doesn't affect what the engine prescribes, but Hevy and the plan disagree until the next week's plan is pushed or an override restates those sets. Worth asking Joe whether he changed a routine by hand.

## Warnings on the current week's plan (week of 2 November)

These came from the plan drawn before Monday's session, so some are already answered by what he logged:

- **Overhead press, three exposures without a gain.** Monday's 8s at RPE 6 should break that; the next prescription should move the load up.
- **Rear delt fly, three without a gain.** Monday's 15s at RPE 8 or under hit the top of the range; the load goes up next time.
- **Band pull-up: set 4 on 1 November logged 4 reps at RPE 10**, below the 5–8 range and over the RPE line, so the load holds — in his case, the band stays. Three exposures without a gain here too. Clears when every set reaches 8 at RPE 8 or under; the written rule then moves him to a lighter band.
- **Negative pull-ups, calf raises (Wednesday and Friday), ab wheel, seated shoulder press, bent-over row: three exposures without a gain each.** Early in a block with a new engine reading old history this is mostly noise; each clears with one session that hits the top of its rep range at the authored RPE.
- **Back squat pinned at 170.5**, more than one rack row above the home anchor of 118. Left, with the reason that the 13 October PT single of 100 kg puts 170.5 at about 75 % of his estimated max, below what the scheme itself proposed. For Joe: 170.5 is the top-set load this Friday.
- **Loads held because there is no usable max to check the RPE against:** goblet squat at 20.25, chest-supported row at 34 (Hevy figure; Joe logged 20 per hand), suitcase carry at 4.25, seated shoulder press at 22.5, split squat at 4.25. These clear once there are logged exposures with reps and RPE to anchor on. The suitcase carry was logged at 0, which isn't a real rack load, so the engine anchored at 5 instead — he needs to log the bell weight.
- **The circuit was flagged as stacked on Monday's lift**, left with the note that it is standing and optional and Joe does it on a spare evening. Note that under the new program the swing session is now a scheduled Monday session, so from next week this rule will look at it properly: it fires if a quality conditioning session falls within 24 hours before a heavy squat or hinge day, or within 6 hours of a lifting session on the same day. Monday swings at RPE 7 before Tuesday's PT legs week could trip it; Joe doing the swings in the evening, well after the morning lift, keeps it quiet.

The old week-plan draft dated 1 November still has one violation (a start load missing) and nine warning kinds; it is superseded and only matters if someone reuses it.

## What Joe needs to agree to

1. **The program change itself.** It is already recorded. He should confirm he's happy with: swings as a separate optional Monday session (12 minutes of 12 swings at 40 lb, growing to 16 minutes then 15 reps), Monday's lift shortened to about 47 minutes, and the pull-up target of 10 weekly sets including negatives and band work. If he'd rather keep the finisher inside the lift, that is a further amendment.
2. **The next week's plan push.** That is the step that writes to Hevy: it will create the swing routine, remove the swing line from Monday's routine, and overwrite whatever hand-edits caused the routine drift. It will ask for his yes on a terminal before anything is written.
3. **Publish.** The export is currently behind the store, so the record on disk doesn't yet reflect version 2 until a publish is run.

Last thing for you to weigh: the pull-up target of 10 against 7 planned sets means the dose check will show him under target by design unless the week plan adds a set to negatives or band pull-ups. Either lower the target to 8, or plan 4 negatives and 5 band sets on Wednesday.

first.text:
Done. Version 2 of your program is in force as of today: same block, same week of the rotation, nothing reset. What's recorded:

- **Monday** is now two sessions. The overhead press session ends at the rear delt flies, about 47 minutes instead of 58. The swings are their own optional session beside it: 12 minutes, a set of 12 at the top of each minute with the 40 lb bell, aiming for a 7. When a session comes in at 7 or easier, it grows by two minutes up to 16, then the reps climb to 15. It never counts against your adherence; it just builds a streak when you do it.
- **Pull-up target is 10 sets a week**, counting negatives and band pull-ups. Your sessions are unchanged.
- **Deadlift stays at 4**, with the reason we agreed written on the version. The Friday single keeps its reason too.
- **Circuit untouched**, and it no longer needs the weekly sign-off.

Nothing has changed in Hevy yet. That happens when next week's plan is pushed, which will create the swing routine, take the swing line off Monday, and ask you before writing anything. Your logged Monday session stays as it is. Publish stays off until plate-pool#52 ships.

Three things to flag, one of them mine:

1. **I need to recheck the pull-up count.** I told you the week plans 11 sets with Sunday's 3 band pull-ups included. The adoption summary counts only Wednesday's 7 and the Friday single. If Sunday's band work isn't being counted, 10 reads under target every week by design, and we either drop to 8 or add a negative and a band set on Wednesday. I'll verify and come back before the next plan is drawn.
2. **Have you edited Monday's routine in Hevy by hand?** Some reps on the press and the row weights don't match the plan. Harmless, and the next push overwrites it, but I'd rather know if it was deliberate.
3. **Timing of the swings.** Tuesday is a PT legs week next week. Hard swings within 24 hours of a heavy squat day will draw a note; doing them Monday evening, well after the lift, keeps that quiet.

From Monday's session: overhead press at 68 lb was too light (8s at RPE 6), so the load moves up next time, as do lateral raises and rear delt flies, both at the top of their range. And log the bell weight on the suitcase carry; it came through as zero.
